intro_html: Stuffed peppers taste great and take forever. You hollow, you par-cook, you stuff, you bake, and then you do it 14 more times. This soup skips every one of those steps and keeps the flavor. Ground turkey, bell peppers, tomato, rice and a savory beef broth base, finished with parmesan. Same dinner, a third of the work.
cost_closing_html: About $3.78 a bowl (at everyday cost). Canned tomatoes and rice keep the base almost free, so nearly every dollar in this pot went to the turkey where it belongs.
shop_smart: Green bell peppers are the cheap ones. Red, yellow and orange peppers are the same vegetable further along and they cost two or three times as much. Green is the right call here.
Canned diced tomatoes and tomato sauce are the base. Buy them by the case when they hit a sale price. They keep for years and they show up in half the recipes on this site.
Rice from the warehouse bag costs almost nothing per serving. That is why it is the carb in so many of these builds. One bag covers this batch and a dozen more.
Worcestershire is the secret in this pot. One bottle lasts a very long time and it is what makes a tomato and turkey soup taste like it simmered all day.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside. Cooking it in the soup turns the whole pot to mush by day three.
Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it goes, until no pink is left.
Add the diced onion and the chopped green bell peppers and cook until they soften, then stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the beef broth, the diced tomatoes with their juice, the tomato sauce and the Worcestershire sauce.
Add the bay leaves, dried oregano and dried thyme, bring it to a simmer, and let it go for 25 to 30 minutes so the peppers go tender and the flavors settle.
Fish out the bay leaves, season with salt and black pepper, and stir the grated parmesan in off the heat.
portion_html: Scoop the cooked rice into your 14 containers first, then set the full soup pot on your scale, subtract the empty pot weight from Step 1, divide by 14, and ladle that exact weight over the rice. Every serving lands near 581 calories with 34 grams of protein.
upsell_html: All the stuffed pepper flavor, none of the stuffing, for about $3.78 a bowl (at everyday cost). This is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Ground turkey, green bell peppers, tomato and rice in a savory broth with parmesan. A 14 serving stuffed pepper soup built for cheap meal prep.
head.keywords: stuffed pepper soup, ground turkey soup, budget meal prep, tomato rice soup, cheap dinner ideas, turkey recipes
steps: Cook the rice separately and set it aside.
Brown the ground turkey in olive oil in a large pot.
Add the onion, bell peppers and garlic and cook until softened.
Pour in the beef broth, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, Worcestershire and herbs, then simmer 25 to 30 minutes.
Season, stir in the parmesan off the heat, and serve over the rice.
